tips.comment: The question, as always in the Oaks, is will the favorite stay. Desert Flower is the best filly on form as she is unbeaten in all her 5 previous races, including the UK 1000 Guineas. She is a daughter of Night Of Thunder and should stay and handle softer ground.

Ryan Moore has deserted Whirl in favour of Minnie Hauk and he rarely gets it wrong, but Whirl was very impressive in the Musidora at York and through in a line with Secret of Love and Smoken comes out the much better horse, albeit Smoken ran well below par in the Musidora. The favourite Desert Flower is clearly a very good horse and would beat these easily over a mile, but her pedigree gives her only a small chance of seeing this mile and a half trip out.

‘Desert Flower’ is the short-price favorite for the ‘Oaks’ classic, but I’ll take a chance on the unexposed selection at a better price. He was only 2L behind that runner in the recent 1000 Guineas, which was just his second career start and a first run after an 8-month break. Any improvement would put him in the mix. There are question marks about the 12f trip for the favorite, while the well-bred selection shouldn’t have any problems.

The French raider is the standout in this Group 1. The 4-year-old has 4 wins from 9 and has been a runner-up 4 times. He was a close 2nd of 13 last August, clear of the rest, in the £709K Juddmonte Group 1, losing to the 128-rated Derby winner 'City Of Troy'. Back from a 5-month break during April and was a runner-up in the £2.7 million Sheema Classic - his well-being is fine. He comes here fresh and will be hard to beat.

We haven't seen the best of this one yet as was unraced at a juvenile but was unbeaten as a 3yo including when winning the St Leger on just fourth start. Will want a true test but this trip takes some getting anyway and he might just be a stronger type this season who has his pacemaker in here to ensure a good gallop. Yard have won this 9 times and jockey four in the last 20 years and can improve their runners a ton for a seasonal reappearance. French favourite is much feared but the more rain we get, I'm not a million miles from Epsom and are getting plenty, the more I like the deeper stamina of Jan Breughal. Has to improve to beat the classy French raider, especially on a line through Deira Mile but he will, and can prove a tough nut to crack as after just 5 career starts could well prove a Group 1 horse this year.

Seventh in last year's Derby here and a former course winner, winning over a mile and a quarter here in April 2024. Stayed on well when winning over this trip at Newmarket last time out and could go well at a decent price for each-way appeal.

Multiple Group and Listed places last season between 7f and 6f. Returned to action with a decent 3rd on ground possibly too quick for him, behind Cosmic Year who since finished 2nd in the Irish 2k Guineas. Followed that up with a French Listed win. Has a penalty to concede to some of these now; however, it doesn't appear an overly strong race and the ground on the softer side will suit.

The 3yo won at the start of the year in Meydan. Excuses on his UK return five weeks ago but not disgraced - very fast ground, decent 10 runner Group 3 contest and he was far too keen in the first half of the race. He’s best judged on his 20 runner £193K sales race win last Sept, the runner-up won the French Derby last weekend. He has ability, top yard/jockey and should be capable of winning at this Listed level.

Won on debut as a 2yo for Sir Michael Stoute and had subsequent 3yo Listed winner Qilin Queen well beat there and won again on next start when making all at Leicester. Finished 2yo career with a fourth of five in the Group 2 Rockfel and can hopefully strip fitter on Friday for seasonal reappearance in the Fred Darling, her first start for the Balding yard. Switch in stable no negative considering trainer and jockey worth following around here. Murphy rides this place really well and was 13 wins from 33 rides for a healthy plus £41.10 lsp here last season and is 21-76 for a return of plus £24.98 lsp here for the last 5 years. Formal goes on any ground and 7f trip is fine so must be a player for jockey who won this race last year. Owner also worth following with their fillies and mares at this meeting too.

I loved the way this one went through the race at Goodwood to win a shade cosily from Logi Bear who has franked the form since. Well entered up and is highly thought of and should handle Epsom seeing as Goodwood is an undulating course too. Yard won this race a couple of years ago and I've been watching this one's price collapse all week so the 7-1 nicked looks value now! Shaped at Goodwood as if an extra furlong would help as doing all of his best work late on and won despite looking a big baby. Yard hardly been on fire but had a nice winner on Monday and could have a nice one on their hands here.

The 2yo was well supported when winning on his debut during March, a 17 runner £21K novice stakes and seems well regarded in the yard. Plenty to like how he picked up 2f out and saw the race out - maybe not the best track position that day. The forecast rain on Thursday will be a plus. He comes here fresh for this conditions race after 11 weeks off the track and you could expect plenty more improvement.

Botanical has been running well in defeat in Listed races and has been dropped a couple of pounds by the handicapper. Epsom is a track where top weights do well due to the undulating, turning nature of the track and horses can never get up to top speeds. With Ryan Moore booked you would hope he has a great chance.

Going to get this one in early. Backed this on debut last year at 150-1 and it won (and on here I believe) as well as an EW Lucky-15, which pretty much set me up for the year. Has been very consistent ever since, the last three over 1m, but looks more suited, in my opinion, to further and has run well over 1m4f. This race will also be fine (1m 2f) as she is better when coming late and will not mind any rain and change in the going. Trainer has had 3 runners at Epsom with a record of 2nd, 3rd, and 4th, so not bad and makes this one a decent EW play.

21 runs, 3 wins and 10 placed efforts tells us Rathgar is pretty consistent and gets in here at the foot of the weights bar one. He seems to cope with quirky tracks if I can call Chester, Goodwood and here at Epsom quirky. Also versatile regarding underfoot conditions so everything is in place for a bold show.

Previous distance winner. Top jockey Hollie Doyle takes the ride. Plum stall draw in 1, so can have a nice prominent early position. Dropping down the handicap and has a nice mark to work with. Each way chance.

The 4yo is on top of his game, three runs this year, going close each time, all on the AW. He was 2nd of 14 last time out, beaten just a nse in a useful £34K handicap, and comes here fresh after a seven week break. Facing some stronger rivals in this handicap but he’s on a nice looking mark. The return to turf might give him a little spark, a couple of decent runs as a youngster in Group company on turf. Not a great draw but is worth an EW shout.

The 5yo progressed nicely last year. Decent run on his return during March in the 22 runner £77K Lincoln handicap - poor draw that day. He’s been kept fresh for this £38K handicap with a 10 week break. Just one previous run at this tricky track, a close 2nd over this C/D as a youngster. He’s on a decent mark, the forecast rain, low draw and strong jockey booking are all positives.

Last year's winner Two Tempting is very tempting but is in a much stiffer mark here and will do well to fend off some unexposed sorts here. The one I like most is this one who won over C&D last time and looks most progressive. Half brother to the tip top Grade 1 winner Bradsell and must have more to come. Has placed form on softish ground but dam was a 7f Listed winner on heavy ground so there is a good chance this one will relish conditions and is already proven at the track. Early booking at a low weight of Hollie Doyle knocked my eye out earlier in the week and the 12-1 voucher is burning a hole in my proverbial pocket now! Still looks value as has so much in his favour. Big shout from fair draw.

Dropping back a small amount in trip looks like a good move. Drops 1lb for being beaten by 6l at Newmarket. Top jockey Rossa Ryan is on board and has ridden him before, so a good partnership. Wide open looking race, so should have an each-way shot.

Solid and progressive form from the 4yo filly last year. Two starts in 2025 and she was a nice class 2 handicap winner five weeks ago, the front two pulling clear and I feel the jockey saved a little that day. No reason why she can’t take another step forward. Being a previous C/D winner last year is a plus. Top jockey in the saddle.

One of my favourite Epsom horses in recent years and won this race last year to add to his 2021 success in this race too. Has slipped back to same winning mark at last year and has been prepped to peak now. Ran a similar race at Chester last time as he did last year on his way to winning this and looks a bombproof EW banker. 7f on this specialist track is ideal for him and we know he'll handle conditions better than most. I'm not too far from Epsom and the more rain that falls the more I love his chances. Saved the Nap till the last race and surely hits the frame at the very very least with conditions sent from above as if someone listened to trainer's plea!!! Trainer in fair form and should have him spot on for this.

7f at Epsom has a small bias for the low stalls and a more pronounced bias for being a front runner. 3rd best track in the country for front runners over the 7f. To my eye, there's only two real front runners in here: Partisan Hero and Legal Reform. Legal Reform, as an 8yo with the highest OR he's ever had, can't possibly be a bet really, so it only leaves the one. 5yo, so has a maturity advantage over some of these, hasn't been out of the first 3 since May 24 and ran his best race to date when 2nd behind Two Tempting at Chester. Had to cover more ground than the winner there and was only beaten in the last couple strides to finish 0.75L behind. That was 7.5f, so the drop to 7f may suit even more. Up 3lbs as a result of the last day, however, with conditions to suit, should really be in the places if producing a repeat.

An Epsom specialist with 4 wins over course and distance. 4th behind the re-opposing winner, Rhoscolyn, in this race last year beaten 3 lengths off a mark of 82. Could go well off a 6 pound lower mark.
Green Impact disappointed in the 2000 Guineas at Newmarket but went there without a run and probably needed the race. He looks the class horse in this Listed event.

Paddy Twomey (SR 18%) trained Currawood is chanced to beat Jessica Harrington trained favourite (and 2,000 Guineas sixth) Green Impact. The selection has been a steady improver in maiden company and ran out a comfortable five length winner at Cork in April. Second to the useful Officer at the Curragh a month ago at Listed level. That horse is a key formline (via Fields Of Gold and the Irish and English 2,000 Guineas). Currawood receives 5lbs from the likely favourite here and looks the better value of the two at current prices.

Formerly trained by Andre Fabre in France and has had two runs since moving to Ger Lyons in Ireland. Finished eighth of nine in the first run in the Listed Devon Stakes at Naas in March following a layoff of over a year. Last time out, won over 7 furlongs at Tipperary, kept on well in the closing stages. Will be suited by today's trip.

Value odds in this bet for Eastwatch, which only raced twice, being runner-up in debut and later winner, and is very lightly weighted. Though possible, it will not be easy to win in this company, but it is likely that the pick will make the frame.

At a massive price, I'm going to chance this J Nallen runner, Cristal Clere, which goes up in distance. With the trainer not coming here for nothing, normally with 3 from 6 wins, he must think something of it in this Listed contest. E/W.
Layfayette was second here in October off a 107 in listed company. Although at the back of the pack on the return last month, I would expect a step forward now second up off a 106 each way.
Minerva will have high expectations given the huge price tag. O'Brien won a similar race with a newcomer yesterday, but Moore will hope this one can get the job done a little bit more comfortably.

It is probably sufficient to note that Ryan Moore has chosen to ride Acapulco Bay, of Aidan O'Brien's two colts, in this three-year-old Listed Event. He drops down in class from running in a Group 3 Derby Trial here last time.

IMPRESSIVE winner last time. Not sure what he beat, but he forged clear from 2f out, looking better the further he went. Steps up in class, which he deserves the chance, and over this longer trip, which should suit.

Improved significantly on her first run of the year at the Curragh when winning in good style at Cork last month. She'll need to take a further step forward now upped in trip and grade, but she's going the right way, and the five pounds sex allowance she receives from the colts could prove crucial.

Aidan O'Brien runs two in this Listed race over twelve furlongs. Ryan Moore is on Alcapulco Boy, who he was on when winning at The Curragh. He has ridden Rock Of Cashel once, and this was on debut outing in eighth place. Since then, Wayne Lordon has been in the saddle, except on the last run where G Ryan was in the saddle. Rock of Cashel has taken in some deep races, possibly been used to set the gallop for other stablemates. He looks to be lining up in his own right for a chance of success. He is sired by Wootton Bassett and dam sire is Galileo, pedigree of top quality like most from this stable. He is having his third run of the season, and the drop in class and step up in trip looks tailor-made for him to express himself with a big run and outpointing his stablemate and others with a big run appearing.

Got off the mark when upped to this trip in a Cork handicap in April (soft) and was even better when 2nd to an improver at Navan (good 1m5f). Great versatility on ground conditions and there's no doubt over stamina. Great chance to feature in the top 3.
Bay Colony stepped up to win at Limerick. She has more on in this higher contest taking on males. Nice type with distance experience and has a place chance.

Big step up in class on the face of it but would surely have won with a clear passage over this C&D last time out and bred to be better than anything we have seen thus far. Worth a small ew dabble at these odds in an open race.

A previous all-weather winner at Dundalk, Titanium Emperor arrives here making a second outing since making the switch from the AW. He showed enough promise last time out when he took an early lead before getting caught. But with that experience under his belt, I think he can go even better here and go close.

Ran to form, beaten 7L in fifth in a race over 10f at Roscommon last time. Will probably come on for that run. Well in on the ratings and form, and now back to a more suitable distance IMO. Therefore, NAP today.

Pierre Royal should confirm the Gowran form with Daler from his first race when they were 2nd and 3rd to Aidan O'Brien's First Wave. Albeit, he is now on six pounds worse terms, having comfortably won at Gowran since over a mile in a second slower time than First Wave's win. So it was an improved run from Pierre Royal, and his mark of 88 seems generous.

Ja'marr is possibly better on the all-weather at Dundalk but is still a capable performer. He could bounce back from underperforming last time at Cork when a beaten favorite in an apprentice handicap. Should get at least a place.

Had a couple of quick starts in April after returning from a 7-month absence. Finished 3rd at Gowran before finishing in midfield at Naas over the same trip and on handicap debut just 5 days later. Stepped up considerably on that effort when beaten less than a length back in maiden company at Gowran last time, over a mile. Is back in handicap company here, from a slightly lower mark and expected to go close going up in trip.

07/05 - First run for six months when 3rd of 9 in an 8f maiden at Gowran a month ago. Was keeping on steadily all the way up the home straight and has to be of interest here, up slightly in trip for handicap debut.
Back after a gelding operation. Looks on a good mark and Billy Lee booked by the in form Prendergast yard. Definite each way appeal though race fitness has to be taken on trust after 3 months off.

ECHINACEA is a likely improver up in trip with stamina on her dam side. That should serve her well ahead of her handicap debut today and the market appears to have overlooked this three year old filly taking on her own age group feasibly treated for this sphere of racing.
May drift as he has his first run for 10 months. Keane has been on top for all 3 of the selection's runnings for Mullins and has been placed off this mark last season.

Trainer Gerard O'Leary (SR 17%) had a close second at 25-1 in a Premier Handicap yesterday. The market is keen on Zipster. The 4yo by Zoustar has been getting closer with each run, pretty much, in four starts for this trainer (formerly UK-based with the Crisfords; won two races for them at a mile. Those wins off marks of 69 and 70.) Dropped 2 lbs today down to OR71 despite a good run over a trip further than this two weeks ago. This is an open race but Zipster looks on the verge of scoring his first win for in-form yard. Good draw in stall 5. Shane Foley rides.

Loingseoir has been hanging out in the mid division and back, but running on. So if it does that today here on this track, I don't think it will do anything. It has a plum draw in 6 under the same pilot, N Burns, after dropping a pound or two. It has a big chance today.

Hit with a five pounds rise for narrow win at Gowran Park in only her second handicap. Higher mark didn't prevent the filly from performing creditably in four further races, signing off with a one length third at Navan, when sporting a visor. Makes her seasonal debut today without the headgear, but will race with a tongue strap. Now only two pounds above her winning mark and has each way potential at fair double figure odds.

Unterberg is still a maiden after 13 starts on turf, but he has twice finished second in Cork handicaps. The first time was over 9 furlongs last August, and he repeated that when beaten by 1 length there last month. He is off the same mark here and must have a good each-way chance with 5 places on offer.

Kaptain Bay has been performing well over hurdles with a 2nd place and a win in his last two races. He returns to the flat off a decent mark of 71 over a shorter distance than the 12f he ran his last two flat races over.

Strong win bet this. Won with a fair bit in hand last time, despite having been outpaced mid-race and getting up on the line. This step up in trip, along with an assured strong pace, will play to his strengths.

Dark Viper finally lost his maiden tag on his penultimate race, having finished 2nd seven times last season and also first time out this season. Not so good last time, 3rd of 6 having been put up 5 pounds, but he is now dropped two pounds back and should still be competitive.

First run for new stable. Very interesting off lower rating, gelded, middle of 2024. 86 now, was at height when won 93. Stable in good form. Ground probably too testing when beaten over 7L at Doncaster last time each way.

Trained by Adrian McGuinness and ridden by apprentice J A Powell, this six-year-old gelding has demonstrated consistent form that suggests he could be competitive here. Notably, he secured a victory at Dundalk on 12 January 2025 in a Class 6 handicap over 7 furlongs, showcasing his potential when conditions suit. In his most recent outing on 25 May 2025 at the Curragh, Exquisite Acclaim finished tenth in a Class 4 handicap over 7 furlongs, beaten by 6 lengths. Prior to that, he was unplaced at Naas on 5 May 2025 over the same distance, indicating a need to recapture his earlier form. His form figures suggest he has the ability to be competitive at this level. 
The return to Leopardstown's turf surface, where he has previously performed well, could play to his strengths. With J A Powell's 7lb claim, he receives a weight advantage that may enhance his competitiveness. 
Given his recent performances and the race conditions, Exquisite Acclaim presents as a viable each-way option for those seeking value in this contest.

Showed some promise on his racecourse debut over a mile at Gowran, finishing in midfield without having too hard a race. Ran a similar race back there next time when again finishing in midfield. Stepped up on those runs with a 4th place finish in a 10f maiden at Ballinrobe last time. Can hopefully improve enough to feature making handicap debut back down in trip.

Strong each-way bet on this one. Wiley Harrington has seen to it that this one has been ridden with handicaps in mind. Not given a hard time on two handicaps to date. Drops to 62 here, and this could well be a target race.

Alan McIntyre’s MOONHALL LASS has a pop at a mile today. Based on her performance LTO in Roscommon, keeping on well inside the dying stages, suggests to my untrained eye she might need that extra furlong. Adding to that, that’s 2 x 0-90s she’s run well in now, boxing above her division 65 rated. This drop to the 0-70 grade with the handicapper shaving off another 2lb could be what the doctor ordered. If they punted this filly 16/1-11/2f LTO in that grade, they’ll surely fancy this today, if she stays the mile of course.

Progressive in three maidens, the latest over 7f at the Curragh when keeping on steadily under a mainly hands and heels ride to finish 6th of the 12 runners. Starts off in handicaps from a fair-looking mark and worth a second look.

Trainer John Joseph Murphy has a good chance here with The Dark Baron, who finished down the field under an extremely restrained ride over six furlongs at Roscommon when making his handicap debut last month. Today, he gets in here off a three lb lower and steps up to a mile for the first time, which should help, as should a more positive ride from stable jockey Joey Sheridan.

I wasn’t planning to get involved in this contest, but a good friend & fellow tipster had me take a second look - and from a price perspective alone, WIDELY ACCLAIMED looks far too tempting to ignore at current odds of 20/1. This 3-year-old colt, trained by Ado McGuinness, was only a length behind MOONHALL LASS - today’s shorter-priced rival - just 24 days ago at Roscommon (7½f, Good), where the latter was backed into favouritism.
A Son of ACLAIM, WIDELY ACCLAIMED finished a staying-on 5th that day and now drops 3lbs in the weights, which could prove key. He steps up slightly in trip here, and that move looks a positive on the back of his closing effort last time out.
McGuinness might have only the one recent winner, but he boasts an impressive 38.89% strike rate for runners hitting the frame in the past fortnight. Retained rider Adam Caffrey - who knows this horse well - has a solid 30.77% place strike rate for the yard over the past year.
Given the form lines, weight drop, and encouraging trainer/jockey stats, I’d be kicking myself if I didn’t have at least a small play at these odds.

Three runs for a mark on the AW but did much better on handicap and turf debut at Roscommon last time out. That was from a 3lb higher mark over half a furlong shorter. She did the best of her work late on there, so the longer trip is going to suit her well.

MICASSO is a three year old who has been catching the eye in behind those placed in recent oiutings. He should benefit from this step up to a mile handicapping and he is well drawn for early track position taking in this left-hand turn. Dangerous at rewarding odds if he gets a run as second reserve overnight.
Johnny Murtagh sticks on the cheekpiece here on Amber Blossom, which may have a positive effect. It's on a good mark for this and looks a lively outsider.

In a very open finale Noel Meade's Your Call is a tentative each way selection. His best form has been on the all weather but on the best of that form he is on a very good mark here. He's also well drawn and the jockey booking looks significant.

Going nap on another Jessica Harrington runner here with Shane Foley on board. Instant Appeal, who is lightly raced for a four-year-old, ran well enough when third last time at Naas. If improving on that run, he could certainly be involved in the finish here tonight.

Trained by Andrew Slattery and ridden by Andrew Joseph Slattery, this four-year-old gelding has demonstrated consistent form that suggests he could be competitive here. In his most recent outing on 18 May 2025 at Naas, Killeaney Bear finished second in a handicap over 1 mile, beaten by 3¾ lengths. Prior to that, he was second at Cork on 10 May 2025 in a maiden hurdle over 2 miles and 1 furlong, indicating his versatility across different race types. Notably, he secured a victory at Leopardstown on 8 August 2024 in a handicap over 1 mile and 1 furlong, showcasing his potential when conditions suit. His form figures suggest he has the ability to be competitive at this level. 
The return to Leopardstown's turf surface, where he has previously performed well, could play to his strengths. With the experience gained from his recent runs and a return to a course he favors, he could be poised to deliver a strong performance.

Back after a 5-month break to lose out by the narrowest of margins at Ballinrobe over 9.6f in May and might well have won had he made his run a little earlier. A very poor start, having got worked up in the stalls, cost him any chance he might have had at the Curragh last time. If that proves to be a one-off, a similar performance to that previous effort at Ballinrobe sees him go close.

Eastern Wind is up in class and down in distance here but could still go close off bottom weight. She has won her last two races which were a 12f handicap at Bellewstown followed by a maiden hurdle at Tipperary.
